title: Vortex-core size and quantum geometry in flat-band superconductors
abstract: We investigate the real-space vortex structure of a flat-band superconductor described by the attractive Hubbard model on the Mielke checkerboard lattice. Using a momentum-space mean-field analysis, we derive a closed-form expression for the coherence length in terms of the quantum metric of the Bloch states and a particle-hole-symmetric pair density. Self-consistent Bogoliubov-de Gennes calculations on a finite disk confirm this prediction across a wide range of fillings and interaction strengths. The coherence length is minimized at half filling, diverges toward both band edges as the pair density vanishes, and depends only logarithmically on the interaction strength. These features differ qualitatively from the conventional BCS picture, which relies on a well-defined Fermi surface and a kinetic mechanism for pair transport. Instead, the vortex-core size is governed by a geometric pair mass arising from virtual interband processes encoded in the quantum metric. Our results establish the vortex core as a direct real-space manifestation of flat-band quantum geometry.
summary: The paper investigates vortex cores in flat-band superconductors using the attractive Hubbard model. It finds that the characteristic size of these cores is not determined by standard Fermi surface physics but instead emerges directly from the underlying geometric structure (quantum metric) of the electronic bands. This establishes a novel link between quantum geometry and superconducting properties.
main_problem: To determine the characteristic spatial scale (coherence length) of superconducting inhomogeneities, such as vortex cores, in flat-band superconductors where conventional BCS theory fails due to the lack of a well-defined Fermi surface.
main_result: The coherence length is governed by a 'geometric pair mass' arising from virtual interband processes encoded in the quantum metric, establishing the vortex core size as a direct real-space manifestation of flat-band quantum geometry.
method: A combination of momentum-space mean-field analysis and self-consistent Bogoliubov-de Gennes (BdG) calculations performed on a finite disk was used to compare theoretical predictions with real-space profiles.
model_or_system: The system is a flat-band superconductor modeled by the attractive Hubbard model on the Mielke checkerboard lattice. The analysis uses mean-field approximations derived from the underlying Hamiltonian, leading to quasiparticle spectra dependent on band structure and pairing gap.
key_observables: Coherence length ($\xi$), superconducting order parameter profile $\Delta(r)$, local particle density $ho(r)$, and the quantum metric tensor $g_{k,ij}$.
important_parameters: Filling ($F$), interaction strength ($U/t$), and the ratio of band energies to pairing gap.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes uniform pairing initially, and later relies on mapping continuum momentum-space results onto real-space BdG calculations using specific cutoffs for consistency.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the flat band structure, self-consistent solutions for $\Delta_0$ and $\mu$, radial profiles of $\Delta(r)$ and $ho(r)$ showing vortex core formation, and comparisons between momentum-space estimates ($\xi_B$) and real-space BdG results ($\xi_v$).
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the model (Hubbard/Mielke lattice) to deriving mean-field equations in momentum space. It then calculates self-consistent solutions for the gap and chemical potential, culminating in solving the full real-space BdG equations on a disk to extract the vortex core size.
why_interesting: This work provides a concrete theoretical framework demonstrating how geometric properties (quantum metrics) can dictate macroscopic superconducting behavior (vortex structure) when conventional kinetic energy mechanisms fail, which is highly relevant for understanding exotic superconductivity in engineered quantum materials.

figures.caption: FIG. 1: (a) Schematic of the two-orbital Mielke checker- board lattice, with sublattices labeled A and B. The lat- tice spacing and hopping amplitude are denoted by a and t, respectively. (b) Band structure of the lattice, showing the flat band (red) and the dispersive band (blue). The shaded region indicates the low-energy continuum sector retained in our analysis, bounded by the cutoff energy Ec and projected onto the radial momentum k = |k|.

FIG. 2: Self-consistent zero-temperature solutions of (a) the pairing gap ∆0 and (b) the chemical potential µ ob- tained from Eqs. (11) and (12). In the weak-coupling limit (U/t →0), both quantities exhibit exact particle- hole symmetry about F = 0.5, corresponding to a half- filled flat band.

FIG. 4: (a) Radial profile of the superconducting or- der parameter ∆(r) for several interaction strengths U. The corresponding bulk momentum-space values are in- dicated by dotted horizontal black lines for comparison. (b) Local particle density ρ(r) for the same parameters. The inset shows a zoom near the vortex center (r = 0), highlighting the finite core density arising from localized bound states. All results are obtained at fixed bulk filling F = 0.49.

(a) Filling depen- dence at fixed U = 0.5t: ξv/a shows a pronounced min- imum at half-filling (F = 0.5) and diverges toward both band edges (F →0 or 1), consistent with the F −1/2 B scaling of Eq. (14). (b) Interaction dependence at fixed F = 0.49: ξv/a varies only weakly with U/t, reflecting the logarithmic factor in Eq. (14).
